label: rem:surreal-bounds-graded-mikusinski
title: Surreal-bound family as graded-Mikusiński std-collapse instances
html:
Remark (the surreal-bound family as graded-Mikusiński std-collapse instances).

The four millennium-problem surreal bounds (rem:bsd-surreal-bound, rem:rh-surreal-bound, rem:p-vs-np-surreal-bound, rem:collatz-surreal-bound) share a structural mechanism. The standard-part map \mathrm{std} \colon \mathbf{No} \to \mathbb{R} collapses a transfinite cost on the surreal-envelope side to a standard-real cost on the archimedean side, leaving a finite gap. Per lem:surreal-squeeze, the gap forces the inequality.

The graded-Mikusiński correspondence (conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence) identifies these four remarks as the same construction at different depths of the iterated-integral filtration on \mathcal{H}_q:

Bound Conjecture interpreted Depth class Std-collapsed object
RH thm:quantum-gap-collapse \mathcal{P}_1 (logs) \zeta critical-line vanishing
BSD conj:q-birch-swinnerton-dyer \mathcal{P}_2 (regulators) L-function rank match
P vs NP conj:p-vs-np-qou \mathcal{P}_{\geq 1} (transfinite Reeb period) budget separation
Collatz conj:q-collatz \mathcal{P}_2 (Bloch–Wigner shadow) contact-boundary deviation

The depth assignment above is conjectural modulo conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence. The correspondence generates all four bounds via the single form:

\mathrm{std}\!\left( \text{depth-}n \text{ infinitesimal cost in } \mathbf{No} \right) > \text{standard archimedean budget},

where n ranges over the four classes and \mathrm{std} serves as the archimedean realization. The inequality direction is enforced by lem:surreal-squeeze.

Unifying the four bounds provides three concrete consequences. First, we replace problem-specific squeezes with a universal std-collapse at a specified depth, analogous to Mikusiński's (1959) field of fractions unifying operational identities. Second, closing the squeeze at depth n for one millennium problem transports to any other problem at the same depth (e.g., depth-2 techniques for BSD \leftrightarrow Collatz). Third, the correspondence predicts a depth-3 surreal bound for any open problem whose archimedean reading involves weight-3 Goncharov periods (multiple zeta values \zeta(3), \zeta(2,1)), such as Apéry-style irrationality questions (Zagier 1986).

We relate this to graded Titchmarsh. Mikusiński passes from C[0,\infty) to its field of fractions via Titchmarsh's no-zero-divisor theorem. The graded analog asks at which iterated-integral depth the *_q-product on \mathcal{H}_q first acquires zero divisors. Each surreal-bound remark is an obstruction to inverting a depth-n element, representing exactly the obstruction Mikusiński removes by passing to fractions. The four bounds are instances of graded Titchmarsh failure, each occurring at its characteristic depth.

The novel mathematical content resides in conj:gb-depth-period-correspondence and its discharge targets.
